title: GGK Commercial Publisher Privacy Policy
intro: The Gifted Girl Kim LLC ("we," "us," or "our") operates GGK Commercial Publisher, an internal creator and publishing tool. This privacy policy explains how GGK Commercial Publisher uses Google/YouTube API Services and how related information is handled. This policy is only for GGK Commercial Publisher. It is not the privacy policy for AI Fitness 411 or any other mobile app.

blocks.text: GGK Commercial Publisher is owned, developed, and operated by The Gifted Girl Kim LLC. The tool is used internally by the owner/developer to prepare and publish owner-approved commercial videos.
GGK Commercial Publisher is an internal publishing tool. It is not offered as a third-party YouTube publishing service for other creators or the public.

After an operator approves a specific rendered commercial file, the tool can upload that exact approved video to an authorized YouTube channel using YouTube Data API v3. A private YouTube upload has been tested successfully. Public or scheduled YouTube release is not treated as available unless YouTube's API project restrictions allow it.
Uploading requires an approved Renderer render identifier. The tool does not substitute a different or newest render for an approved one.

sections.heading: Use of Google / YouTube API Services

blocks.text: GGK Commercial Publisher uses Google OAuth 2.0 and YouTube Data API v3 to connect an authorized Google/YouTube account and, when the operator confirms an upload, to send an approved commercial video and related metadata to YouTube.
The currently authorized account is the owner's own YouTube account/channel.
GGK Commercial Publisher's use of information received from Google APIs adheres to the Google API Services User Data Policy, including the Limited Use requirements.

sections.heading: Google / YouTube Information That May Be Accessed

blocks.text: When an operator connects YouTube, GGK Commercial Publisher requests these OAuth scopes:

items: YouTube read access (youtube.readonly), used to identify the authorized channel
YouTube video upload access (youtube.upload), used to upload an approved commercial video to that channel

blocks.text: From the authorized YouTube account, the tool may obtain basic channel identity information: channel ID and channel title. The tool does not request or store a Google account email address as part of this YouTube connection.

When an operator confirms an upload, the tool sends the approved video file plus a title and description to YouTube. YouTube may return a video ID and privacy status. While the YouTube connection remains authorized, the tool may store that video ID as part of the publishing record and may read status information for videos it already uploaded, for example to confirm that a video remains private.
Channel ID and channel title are used only to confirm which authorized YouTube channel is connected and to show that connection status to the operator.

Video upload access is used only to upload an owner-approved commercial to that authorized channel after an explicit operator confirmation. Tokens are used only to complete those authorized Google/YouTube API calls.

sections.heading: How OAuth Credentials and Tokens Are Secured

blocks.text: OAuth access tokens and refresh tokens are stored in the Windows Credential Manager and protected with Windows DPAPI on the GGK host. They are not shown in the Operator Console.
Publisher JSON records are written so they do not contain OAuth access tokens, refresh tokens, or client secrets. Public API responses are checked so secret-shaped token values are not returned.

sections.heading: Account Metadata That May Be Stored

blocks.text: While YouTube is connected, GGK Commercial Publisher may store the following locally on the GGK host:

items: Google/YouTube Authorized Data: channel ID, channel title, granted OAuth scopes, token expiry, and any YouTube video ID returned by the API
GGK-owned publishing/audit data: job IDs, approval IDs, render IDs, project IDs, operator-authored titles and descriptions, intended privacy/status, timestamps, and a flag that an upload occurred
Non-sensitive local identifiers: local account ID, platform name, connection status, connected/disconnected timestamps, and an opaque vault reference that is not the token itself
Safe last-error text, if a connection or upload fails

blocks.text: OAuth access tokens and refresh tokens are stored only in the Windows vault, not in Publisher JSON.

sections.heading: How Google User Data Is Not Used

items: We do not sell Google user data.
We do not use Google user data for advertising, including personalized advertising, retargeting, or advertising measurement.
We do not share Google user data with unrelated third parties.
We do not use Google user data to train, improve, or develop generalized AI or machine-learning models.

blocks.text: Video files and upload metadata are sent to Google/YouTube so the authorized channel can receive the operator-approved commercial. That sharing is required to provide the YouTube API feature.

GGK Commercial Publisher does not share Google user data with unrelated advertising, analytics, or data-broker services. We may disclose information if required by law or to protect the security of the tool or our legal rights.
OAuth tokens remain in the Windows vault only while YouTube is connected. On disconnect or OAuth revocation, the vault credential is deleted immediately.

Google/YouTube Authorized Data is deleted immediately on disconnect or when authorization can no longer be refreshed. GGK-owned publishing records, local identifiers, commercial projects, render approvals, and locally created MP4 files are retained as internal business/audit records.

Videos uploaded to YouTube remain on YouTube under Google's and the channel owner's YouTube settings and policies. Disconnecting GGK Commercial Publisher does not delete videos already uploaded to YouTube.

The operator can disconnect YouTube from GGK Commercial Publisher. Disconnecting immediately asks Google to revoke the stored authorization token and deletes the locally stored credential from the Windows vault.

At the same time, GGK immediately deletes Google/YouTube Authorized Data from local records: channel ID, channel title, granted scopes, token expiry, and YouTube video IDs. This happens as soon as disconnect or revocation is processed, and in all cases within 7 days.

GGK keeps its own publishing history after disconnect: job IDs, approved render identifiers, operator-authored titles and descriptions, timestamps, and a local flag that an upload occurred. Locally created MP4s, commercial projects, render approvals, and mock publishing history are not deleted because YouTube was disconnected.
Disconnecting does not delete or change videos that were already uploaded to YouTube.

You can also revoke GGK Commercial Publisher's access directly in your Google Account permissions or Google security settings. After Google access is revoked, or if stored tokens can no longer be refreshed, the tool cannot call YouTube APIs until the operator connects again, and remaining Google/YouTube Authorized Data is deleted as described above.
